# Final Touches — Murim Login

## Goal

Prepare one mastered chapter for readers. This pass adds footnotes, repairs formatting, and fixes duplicate or missing sentences. It is not a fluency rewrite.

Keep the mastered prose. Change a sentence only to attach a footnote, repair System / thought / speech / chat formatting, restore a source sentence the English dropped, or remove an English sentence the Korean does not support.

## Duplicates and omissions

Compare the English with the Korean source.

- Restore source facts, events, dialogue, and sentences the English dropped, in the same place in the scene.
- Remove English sentences that have no support in the Korean.
- Keep a bold label that names a quoted document, manual, warning, or sign, such as `> **Warning**`. Keep it when this chapter recalls or reprints a notice that was labeled earlier, even if the Korean reprint shows only the body.
- Keep repetition the Korean itself repeats: comedy, panic, emphasis, echoed dialogue, and short beats such as `……`.
- Do not treat a short refrain or a deliberate echo as a duplicate.

## Footnotes

Use Markdown footnotes (`[^1]`, `[^2]`, …). Number them in order of first appearance, starting at 1 for this chapter. Put every definition in one block at the end of the file.

Within this chapter, write one definition for a term, unit, amount, or reference. Every later occurrence of that same thing reuses the same marker. `goshiwon` five times is one note, and so is `hyung`. A different amount or a different term gets its own note. Another chapter may carry its own note for the same term.

Write notes in factual English. No spoilers and no jokes added by the note. Romanize words. A note may include the original character when it is explaining that character. Keep Hangul jamo already used as chat reactions, such as ㅋㅋ and ㄷㄷ.

Add a note only when an English reader would otherwise miss the meaning or the conversion. Skip it when the sentence already says what the reference means. A translated proverb whose warning is plain, a joke the next line completes, a place name used as a place, and a fictional law the dialogue already describes do not get notes.

Skip a conversion footnote when the prose already states both metric and imperial for that quantity.

### Won

Footnote Korean won, including round figures and vague amounts (“hundreds of millions of won”), when the prose does not already give the conversion. Use only the project rates in the packet. Show dollars, then euros, as approximate figures. Round large amounts to about two significant figures and say “about.” For a vague amount, give the approximate range those words cover. One note per distinct amount; reuse it for every later mention of that same amount.

Do not convert traditional money (nyang, taels, cash) or Chinese yuan with the won rate. Explain those with a cultural or historical note only when the English does not already carry the meaning.

### Units

Footnote a Korean or Chinese traditional unit, or a metric quantity, once in the chapter, with both metric and imperial, using this table:

| Unit | Use | Metric | Imperial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pyeong (평) | area | 3.31 m² | 35.6 ft² |
| geun (근) | Korean weight | 600 g | 1.32 lb |
| ja / cheok (자) | length | 30.3 cm | 11.9 in |
| chi (치) | length | 3.03 cm | 1.19 in |
| don (돈) | weight | 3.75 g | 0.132 oz |
| gwan (관) | weight | 3.75 kg | 8.27 lb |
| ri (리), Korea | distance | 393 m | 0.244 mi |
| li (里), China | distance | 500 m | 0.311 mi |
| jin (斤), modern Chinese | weight | 500 g | 1.10 lb |
| liang (两), modern Chinese | weight | 50 g | 1.76 oz |

Choose Korean ri or Chinese li from the setting. Say which one the note uses.

Also footnote metric quantities already in the English (kilometers, meters, centimeters, kilograms, grams, liters, square meters, degrees Celsius) with the imperial equivalent. Use unit words or abbreviations (`ft`, `in`, `mi`, `lb`, `oz`, `gal`). Do not use `"` or `'` as unit marks.

### Cultural references

Footnote a Korean, Chinese, or other Asian word, custom, institution, food, joke, or allusion when the English does not already carry it: `goshiwon`, `hyung`, `doenjang`, `jeonse`. Explain it in one or two sentences. One note per term in the chapter, reused by every later occurrence.

Leave it unnoted when the English is already clear. Do not explain a proverb the translation has already stated, a pun the scene completes, or ordinary vocabulary.

Do not footnote standing series vocabulary. Never add a note whose job is to define any of these, including ordinary variants and compounds:

- Murim
- qi, including demonic qi, innate qi, and qi deviation
- dantian, including the Upper, Middle, and Lower Dantian
- internal energy
- mana

A note about something else may mention these words. Do not attach a marker to them.

## Formatting

Enforce these four patterns. Repair System, speech, thought, and chat formatting when it drifts. Leave every other blockquote heading as it stands.

- **System.** Each real game System panel is one Markdown blockquote headed exactly `> **System**`. Keep the panel’s lines inside that blockquote. Start a new panel only when prose intervenes. Do not wrap System text in square brackets or label a manual, sign, or ordinary quotation as System. A manual or remembered notice keeps its own label, such as `> **Warning**` or `> **Product User Manual**`. That label is not a System panel, and it is not drift.
- **Speech.** Spoken dialogue uses curly double quotes (`“` `”`). Not straight quotes, not italics.
- **Thoughts.** Direct thoughts are italics with no quotation marks.
- **Chat and comments.** Public comment threads and private chat logs shown as threads are one blockquote. Each message line begins with `└`, as in `> └ **Name:** message`. Keep a thread title that is not itself a message, such as `> **Peace Guild**`, on its own line above the messages. Do not add a `**Chat**` heading. A status line that is only a name or level, such as `> **Lv. 22 Hyuk Mujin**`, is not a chat message. Leave that line unchanged, including the bold. Ordinary spoken dialogue stays in curly quotes.
- **Headings.** The only Markdown heading is `# Chapter N`. Do not add `##` or `###`. A diary title or similar label stays a bold line, `**Training Day 1**`, even when the mastered copy used a smaller heading.

Leave narration as narration. Scene breaks stay `* * *`, with the same count as the source.

## Output contract

Return only the complete English Markdown chapter. The first nonblank line must be `# Chapter N`. No status line and no model preamble. Do not add Hangul syllables. Chat jamo and a character cited in a note may stay.

## Project conversion rates

These rates are binding. Do not look up or substitute a market rate.

- 1 US dollar = 1400 Korean won
- 1 euro = 1550 Korean won

Convert every won amount with these rates. In each footnote, give dollars first and euros second.

＃181화



“너는 잠시라도 눈을 뗐다 하면 사고를 치는구나.”

가볍게 사제를 꾸짖은 백무성이 우황태를 향해 고개를 숙여 보였다.

“서로 간에 사소한 오해가 있었던 것 같습니다. 넓은 아량으로 용서하시지요.”

인상만큼이나 부드러운 목소리였다.

우황태는 무인이라기보다는 장사치에 가까웠다. 무공은 일류지만 표국을 운영해 오며 길러 낸 눈썰미만큼은 절정이라고 자부할 수 있을 만큼.

아마 평소였다면 백무성을 본 순간 이런 생각을 했을지도 모른다.

‘평범 속의 비범.’

그러나 불행히도 지금의 우황태는 제정신이 아니었다.

난데없이 끼어든 백무성의 멀끔한 인상은 만만해 보였고 공손하면서도 강자의 여유가 묻어 나오는 목소리는 건방지게만 들렸다.

“뭐라, 넓은 아량으로 용서?”

부글거리는 목소리로 뇌까린 그가 눈썹을 치켜떴다.

“감히 누구한테 이래라저래라 하는 것이냐?”

“그런 의도로 드린 말씀은 아닙니다만, 마음이 상하셨다면 사과드리지요.”

“사과? 허, 이 하룻강아지 같은 놈이 그래도.”

까드득.

본래 한 번 분노에 사로잡히면 사고가 흐려지기 마련.

주먹을 말아 쥐며 나서는 우황태를 다른 문주들이 황급히 만류했다.

“우 국주, 이쯤에서 그만하는 것이 좋겠소.”

“송 문주의 말이 옳소이다. 괜히 소란 일으켜 봤자 좋을 게 뭐가 있겠소?”

“어디서 굴러먹다 왔는지 모를 놈들이 건방을 떠는데 참아라? 당신들도 나를 우습게 여기는 거요?”

“아니, 그 말이 아니라.”

“그럼 무슨 말이 하고 싶은 건가?”

이제는 반쯤 하대나 다름없는 말투. 산서오문의 문주들은 내심 눈살을 찌푸렸지만 괜한 분란은 막아야 했다.

“그저 시기와 장소가 틀렸다는 말이오. 우리 처지를 잊은 거요?”

“굳이 하겠다면 더 이상 말리지는 않겠소만…… 태원진가에 미운털이 박힌 이때 소란을 일으킬 필요는 없지.”

“화난 건 이해하지만 우리 입장도 생각해 주시구려. 다 같이 좀 살아 봅시다.”

또, 또. 그놈의 태원진가!

우황태는 순간 터져 나오려는 욕설을 가까스로 참았다. 주위에 수많은 눈과 귀가 없었다면 온갖 욕설을 퍼부으며 눈에 보이는 것들을 전부 때려 부쉈을 것이다.

하지만 마지막 한 줄기 이성이 그를 붙잡았다.

“끄으으응.”

간신히 마음을 진정시킨 우황태가 백무성을 노려보았다. 그는 여전히 침착한 표정으로 그 자리에 서 있었다.

“마음 같아서는 당장 단매에 때려죽여도 시원치 않지만…… 촌무지렁이의 실수라 생각하고 넘어가 주마. 꺼져라, 마음이 바뀌기 전에.”

물끄러미 그를 바라보던 백무성이 고개를 숙였다.

“사정을 봐주셔서 감사드립니다.”

“흥, 운 좋은 놈들.”

그러나 운이 좋은 것은 우황태였다.

백무성이 한발 앞서 전음을 날리지 않았더라면 그는 지금쯤 사경을 헤매고 있었을 테니까.

- 둘째, 멈춰라.

막 몸을 날리려던 매화삼절의 둘째, 패화권(敗華拳) 철우의 신형이 우뚝 멈췄다.

그의 잇새 사이로 다른 이에게 들리지 않는 음성이 새어 나왔다.

- 저로 모자라서 대사형까지 건드린 놈입니다.

- 상관없다.

- 전 상관있습니다. 한 대만, 딱 한 대만 때리면 안 됩니까?

- 때려죽이고 싶다는 말로 들리는구나.

- ……살살 때리겠습니다. 진짜 딱 한 대만요.

- 그건 살살 때려죽이겠다는 말이고. 괜한 시선을 끌지 말라는 사부님의 엄명을 잊었느냐?

갈등하던 철우가 꽉 움켜쥐고 있던 주먹을 늘어뜨렸다.

“후우, 미치겠네.”

백무성이 대견하다는 듯 어깨를 두드려 주었다.

“잘 참았다. 이 또한 수련이다.”

“이게 뭐가 수련입니까? 기껏 배워 놓은 무공도 제때 못 쓰는구먼.”

“무분별한 살생(殺生)은 너를 망칠 뿐이다. 무공은 정기신을 갈고 닦는 것이지, 누군가를 죽이기 위한 게 아니야.”

“사형을 볼 때마다 헷갈립니다. 제가 화산파 제자인지, 소림사 승려인지.”

“네 녀석 성격에 승려가 가당키나 하겠느냐? 앞으로 부숴 먹을 목탁만 불쌍하지.”

피식 웃는 백무성의 모습에 철우가 한숨을 내쉬었다.

마음 깊이 존경하는 사형이지만 너무 사람이 좋아서 문제다.

“저런 놈들은 아구창을 박살 내야 하는 건데…….”

“어허, 그 입!”

“알겠습니다. 알겠어요.”

철우는 어느새 훌쩍 멀어진 우황태의 뒷모습을 바라보며 입맛을 다셨다.

‘얼굴 기억해 뒀다. 한 번만 걸려라.’

그런 사제의 생각을 모를 리 없는 백무성이다. 그는 고개를 절레절레 내저었다.

“허튼 생각은 그만하고 막내부터 찾거라.”

“은향이 그 녀석 또 없어졌습니까?”

“그래, 너처럼 말이지.”

철우가 움찔했다.

“저, 저는 소피보러 간 겁니다.”

“그랬지. 그런데 소피보러 간다는 놈이 왜 사람 많은 곳에서 시비가 붙었느냐?”

“시원하게 비우고 오는 길에 그만. 아니 사형, 지금 저 못 믿으시는 겁니까? 아직 손 안 닦았는데 냄새 맡아 보실래요?”

“……됐다.”

백무성은 관자놀이를 문질렀다. 누구보다 아끼는 사제들이지만 다루기가 여간 까다로운 것이 아니었다.

그나마 철우는 덩치라도 커서 금방 찾지, 막내 사제인 은향은 이런 인파 속에서 보이지도 않는다.

“보이는 것 없느냐?”

남들보다 머리 두 개는 더 큰 철우가 주위를 쓱 훑었다.

“글쎄요. 사람이 워낙 많아서.”

끝도 없이 늘어선 북적이는 인파 속에서 자그마한 체구의 소녀를 찾는 건 절정 고수의 눈으로도 어렵다.

오죽 사람이 많으면 곳곳에 좌판을 깐 장사치들마저 보일 정도였다.

“그나저나 태원진가가 이 정도였습니까? 오기 전까지는 들어 본 적도 없는데.”

“아는 사람은 알지. 현 문주인 산서기협(山西奇俠)도 그렇고, 진천검(振天劍)도 제법 알려져 있지 않느냐?”

“산서기협은 잘 모르겠고 진천검이라면 십봉룡이니 뭐니 하는 그놈 말입니까?”

“그놈이라니. 입조심하거라.”

“학관이나 다니는 샌님인데요, 뭘. 제 생각엔 아마 대사형이 훨씬…….”

“어허. 보기도 전에 사람을 판단하는 고약한 버릇은 어디서 배웠느냐? 그는 분명 뛰어난 인재다.”

“뭐, 산서성에서 그 정도면 개천에서 용 난 것이나 다름없긴 합니다만.”

시큰둥하게 대꾸하던 철우가 문득 눈살을 찌푸렸다.

“그 왜, 진천검 말고도 무슨 용인지 미꾸라지인지, 한 명 더 있지 않습니까?”

“용? 산서잠룡을 말하는 것이냐?”

“아, 맞습니다. 산서잠룡.”

“진천검만큼은 아니지만 제법 뛰어난 기재라고 들었지.”

“용인지 미꾸라진지, 오는 길에 지긋지긋하게 들어서 얼굴이나 한번 봐야겠습니다.”

주먹을 불끈 움켜쥐는 철우를 본 백무성의 입꼬리가 슬쩍 올라갔다.

I could.

*The Jin Family of Taiyuan.*

I was back after three days away.

“I-I went to take a leak.”

“That’s right. But why did someone who went to take a leak end up picking a fight in the middle of a crowd?”

“It happened on my way back after I’d finished. Wait, Senior Brother, do you not believe me? I haven’t washed my hands yet. Want to smell them?”

“…Never mind.”

Baek Museong rubbed his temple. He cherished his Junior Brothers more than anyone, but they were exceptionally difficult to handle.

At least Chulwoo was big enough to find quickly. Their youngest Junior Disciple, Eunhyang, was practically invisible in a crowd like this.

“Do you see anything?”

Chulwoo, who was at least two heads taller than everyone else, swept his gaze around.

“Not really. There are too many people.”

Even a Peak master’s eyes would struggle to find a small girl amid the endless, bustling mass.

The crowd was so large that merchants had even set up stalls here and there.

“By the way, was the Jin Family of Taiyuan always this big? I’d never even heard of it before we came.”

“Those in the know do. The current Sect Leader, the Shanxi Extraordinary Hero, is fairly well known, and so is the Heaven Shaking Sword, isn’t he?”

“I don’t know about the Shanxi Extraordinary Hero, but the Heaven Shaking Sword… Is that the fellow who’s supposedly one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes?”

“Don’t call him that. Watch your mouth.”

“He’s just a bookworm who goes to an academy. In my opinion, Senior Brother is much more…”

“Hey. Where did you learn that nasty habit of judging people before you’ve even met them? He is clearly a remarkable talent.”

“Well, for someone from Shanxi Province, being that good is practically a dragon rising from a ditch.”

Chulwoo answered indifferently, then suddenly frowned.

“Wasn’t there someone else besides the Heaven Shaking Sword? Some other dragon—or was it a loach?”

“A dragon? Do you mean the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”

“Ah, right. The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.”

“I hear he’s quite talented, though not as much as the Heaven Shaking Sword.”

“Dragon or loach, I’ve heard about him nonstop on the way here. I should at least take a look at his face.”

The corner of Baek Museong’s mouth lifted as he watched Chulwoo clench his fists.

“Do you want to spar with him?”

Chulwoo scratched the back of his head.

“Not particularly. I’d win anyway.”

“Competitive spirit is a good thing, but avoid causing trouble if you can.”

“What trouble could there be? Since we came all this way, I just want to see what he can do.”

Baek Museong studied his Second Junior Brother.

Despite what Chulwoo said, his curiosity was obvious.

After spending years cooped up on Huashan, facing the same people every day, he seemed excited to finally be out in the world.

“You’ll see him soon enough. Of course, we need to find the youngest first.”

The final words came out almost as a sigh.

The gates of the Jin Family of Taiyuan were already open, and the invited guests were streaming inside like clouds.

Baek Museong was wondering whether he would have to climb a tree when—

“Senior Brother, it’s all right if I make a little noise, isn’t it?”

“What?”

Chulwoo grinned and drew a deep breath.

The next instant, a thunderous shout erupted.

“Eun—hyang!”

Baek Museong had no time to stop him. Chulwoo’s voice was every bit as tremendous as his body.

The people around them clapped their hands over their ears and dropped to the ground, while the countless people who had been laughing and chatting abruptly fell silent.

As a hush descended over the crowd like a bucket of cold water—

“Big Brothers! I’m over here!”

Far in the distance, Chulwoo spotted a young girl eagerly jumping up and down in place. He spoke triumphantly.

“Ha-ha! Senior Brother, I found her!”

“…Yes, well done. Very well done.”

Baek Museong put a hand to his head.

Just then—

Whoosh.

Hundreds of people began murmuring as they parted like a field of reeds before the wind.

At the end of the open path stood a man like an iron tower. Chulwoo muttered without realizing it,

“Is that a man or a bear?”

“He’s a man. If not for him, the Jin Family of Taiyuan would not be what it is today.”

Baek Museong respectfully offered a cupped-fist salute to the bear-like man, Jin Wikyung.

* * *

Thud-thud-thud-thud!

The scenery whipped past us. Hyuk Mujin, riding beside me, shouted over the pounding hooves.

“We were definitely slow on the way there, but we’re incredibly fast coming back. Is it because we took our time two days ago?”

“Everything happens for a reason.”

“What reason?”

“We move faster when no one tries to stuff his face while riding a horse.”

“Ah.”

Cheongpung had looked gloomy the entire trip. Before we left, I had stopped him from packing a mountain of food.

“I’m hungry.”

I answered coldly.

“Endure it.”

A Peak master’s digestion was Peak-level too. Cheongpung crapped as much as he ate, then ate as much as he crapped.

And since he ate often, he naturally had to crap often…

Damn it. This is disgusting. I’ll stop there.

“How far are we?”

“We just passed the ninth village, so… We should arrive in half a shichen[^2] at the earliest, or one full shichen[^2] at the latest.”

The sunlight pouring down made my eyes sting. I looked up at the sun as it slowly climbed toward the middle of the sky.

“So we’ll arrive around noon?”

“Probably.”

“We’re late, aren’t we?”

“Of course we’re late. Isn’t that why we’re riding like hell, trying to be a little less late?”

Fair point.

Instead of answering, I spurred my horse onward. With every stride, the long bundle strapped across my back thumped against the horse’s back.

*Ugh, what a pain.*

The bundle contained the Unnamed Sword.

I was supposed to have returned it to Jeok Cheongang, but instead, I had somehow ended up taking it back.

As long as I lived in a Murim where the law was damn far away and fists were painfully close, I had no choice.

*It’s not like I can put it in my inventory either.*

I could at least claim I had tucked the Flame Divine Palm martial arts manual inside my clothes. But if an entire sword suddenly popped out of my pocket, there would be no explaining that away.

If I were alone, it might be different. But with other people watching, it would be the perfect way to get accused of practicing demonic, heterodox arts.

*I really got myself into a mess this time.*

It wasn’t that I resented being saddled with a troublesome object. I simply hated the thought of having to meet Fire King Jeok Cheongang—that terrifying old man—again.

“Let’s meet again soon.”

*Meet again, my ass.*

Every time I remembered what he had said a few shichen[^2] ago, my stomach churned.

Hyuk Mujin, who had been sneaking glances at me from time to time, asked,

“Why do you look like that?”

“I was thinking about the Fire King.”

“Ugh. Life’s too short for anything but happy thoughts, so why imagine something that horrible?”

“If you were me, wouldn’t you think about him? He said he’d be back soon.”

“Speaking of which, could you give me some time off? I suddenly miss my family.”

“You bastard. You’re trying to save yourself.”

“You never know what might happen. Before I die, I should at least see my parents’ faces one more time.”

“That doesn’t sound like something an unfilial son who hasn’t shown his face in years should say.”

“I’d like to take this opportunity to become a good son.”

“Nope.”

I dismissed Hyuk Mujin’s bullshit and looked up at the sky with a sigh.

“Even the heavens are heartless. Why did that old man have to leave this thing with me?”

“He said it was a pain to carry around.”

“For such a petty reason?”

“With him, I can completely believe it.”

“…”

That was surprisingly convincing.

“I could lose it before he comes back. Or I could quietly pocket it for myself.”

“You, Captain?”

Hyuk Mujin laughed as if he had just heard a brilliant joke.

“If you were that kind of person, what have you been doing all this time? If you hadn’t been on the verge of death, you probably would’ve just kept the Blazing Flame Divine Pill too.”

“That’s…”

He had a point.

“Just hide it somewhere no one will notice. Who knows? Maybe that great Fire King will teach you a move in return.”

“Teach me, my ass. I’m sure he’d love to teach the man who killed his Disciple.”

The absurdity drew a quiet laugh from me.

The Fire Gate Clan was said to pass its arts down to a single successor and never teach outsiders. Even setting personal feelings aside, the idea that he would teach martial arts to an outsider like me was ridiculous.

“Your nonsense is only funny in moderation, you idiot.”

“Well, now that you mention it, I suppose you’re right.”

At that moment, Cheongpung—who had been drooping like a corpse and endlessly repeating that he was hungry—spoke up.

“Isn’t he trying to take you as his Disciple, Benefactor?”

“…”

“…”

“Maybe not? I think he is. Grandpa Jeok seemed to be watching you closely, Benefactor.”

“Me?”

“Captain?” Hyuk Mujin asked.

Our gazes met in midair. Hyuk Mujin looked utterly baffled. I was probably making the same face.

We both let out disbelieving laughs.

“That’s great. Congratulations in advance, Captain.”

“Yeah. Thanks.”

*Me? Someone he’d known for barely a day or two?*

The idea was so absurd it didn’t even qualify as a joke.

“Maybe not? Or am I right?”

As Cheongpung tilted his head over his own bizarre suggestion, Hyuk Mujin raised a finger and pointed into the distance.

“Can you see it?”

I could.

People were walking down a well-kept road. Farther ahead lay a broad expanse of land surrounded by a teeming crowd.

*The Jin Family of Taiyuan.*

I was back after three days away.
